translationRepairs: His grandfather Jiang Zhan served in the Song as Left Director of the Bureau of Honors and as a Three Ministers of Equal Court Rank.
His grandfather Jiang Zhan served in the Song as Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and as Equal in Ceremonial to the Three Ministers.
左光祿大夫 is a prestige title, not a Bureau of Honors post, and 儀同三司 marks ceremonial equality with the Three Ministers; the replacement renders both accurately.
His father Jiang Nian was a Composition Official and was killed by Liu Ziye (Emperor Taichu).
His father Jiang Nian was a Composition Official and was killed by Taichu.
爲太初所殺 names Taichu as the killing agent, not Liu Ziye; “killed under Taichu” weakens 爲…所殺 into an era setting. Restore the agent as Taichu.
When Prince Guiyang of Xiufan assumed his provincial post, he invited Xiao to serve as Master of Reception, but Xiao declined.
When Liu Xiufan, Prince of Guiyang, assumed his provincial post, he invited Xiao to serve as Master of Reception, but Xiao declined.
桂陽王休範 is the Prince of Guiyang, personal name Xiufan; “Prince Guiyang of Xiufan” inverts title and name. Liu Xiufan is the correct Song princely identity.
He was soon made Attendant of the Masters of Writing on Prince Ancheng's Rapid Cavalry staff.
He was soon made Attendant-in-Ordinary on Prince Ancheng's Rapid Cavalry staff.
驃騎從事中郎 is an adjutant post on the Rapid Cavalry staff, not an office of the Masters of Writing.

Earlier, Jiang Zhan had married a daughter of Chu Xiu and was later dismissed; when Chu Yuan became General of the Guard, he admired Xiao's character, opened relations with him in advance, and appointed him Chief Clerk.

Earlier, Jiang Zhan had married a daughter of Chu Xiu; she was later sent away; when Chu Yuan became General of the Guard, he admired Xiao's character, opened relations with him in advance, and appointed him Chief Clerk.
被遣 after 娶褚秀之女 refers to sending away the wife, not dismissing Jiang Zhan; the proposed “who” clause can attach to Chu Xiu. Make the wife the patient of 被遣.
He was then made Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the staff of the Grand Marshal.
He was then made Attendant-in-Ordinary on the staff of the Grand Marshal.
太尉從事中郎 is a Grand Marshal staff post; Masters of Writing is not in the Chinese.

At the start of the Yongming reign he again served Prince Yuzhang as Adviser to the Grand Marshal and Recorder, then became Companion to Prince Nanjun and Secretary on the staff of Prince Jingling of Jingling.
At the start of the Yongming reign he again served Prince Yuzhang as Adviser to the Grand Marshal and Recorder, then became Companion to Prince Nanjun and Secretary on the staff of Prince Jingling.
The Chinese has only 竟陵王; repeating the fief as “Prince Jingling of Jingling” is an English invention, and dropping the extra “of Jingling” restores the source.
He was promoted to Palace Attendant and also served as provincial Director of Selection for his native commandery.
He was promoted to Palace Attendant and also served as provincial Director of Selection for his native province.
本州 is the native province, not a commandery; the proposed “native province” matches 州.
When Prince Jian'an of Xiuren held Yang Province in the Song, he recruited Chang as provincial Master of Records.
When Prince Jian'an, Xiuren, held Yang Province in the Song, he recruited Chang as provincial Master of Records.
休仁 is the prince’s personal name, not a fief; “Prince Jian'an of Xiuren” treats the name as a place.
When Prince Jianping of Jingsu served as Northern Expedition Commander for Southern Xuzhou, Chang again became his Master of Records and was esteemed for his longstanding integrity.
When Prince Jianping, Jingsu, served as Northern Expedition Commander for Southern Xuzhou, Chang again became his Master of Records and was esteemed for his longstanding integrity.
景素 is the prince’s personal name, not a fief; “Prince Jianping of Jingsu” reverses title and name.
When Emperor Ming took the throne, Xiao was reassigned as Director of the Secretariat and then as tutor to the Prince of Jin'an.
When Emperor Ming took the throne, Xiao was reassigned as Director of the Palace Library and then as tutor to the Prince of Jin'an.
祕書監 is the Palace Library directorate, not the Secretariat (中書/門下).
When Emperor Ming took the throne, Xiao was changed to Director of the Secretariat and then changed to tutor to the Prince of Jin'an.
When Emperor Ming took the throne, Xiao was changed to Director of the Palace Library and then changed to tutor to the Prince of Jin'an.
The same 祕書監 error is in the literal English; Palace Library is the correct office.

The late emperor treated him with affection, and the Founding Emperor regarded him with special favor; whether court nobles or commoners in the countryside, though their knowledge differed in detail, who did not know what had happened?

Emperor Shizu treated him with affection, and Emperor Taizong regarded him with special favor; whether court nobles or commoners in the countryside, though their knowledge differed in detail, who did not know what had happened?
世祖 and 太宗 are Song temple names for the emperors who favored Prince Jianping; 太宗 is not 太祖, already used for the Qi Founding Emperor in the memorial’s address.

The Former Emperor was intimate with him, the Founding Emperor regarded him with special favor; whether court nobles or humble men in the wilds, though what they heard and saw differed, who did not know this affair?
Shizu was intimate with him; Taizong regarded him with special favor; whether court nobles or humble men in the wilds, though what they heard and saw differed, who did not know this affair?
The literal likewise renders 太宗 as Founding Emperor, colliding with 太祖; Shizu and Taizong restore the temple names.

He sought release from Xuzhou to avoid the crucial post at the northern gate; he bitterly begged for Kuaiji, eager to dwell in the idle duties of eastern Yong—this all is manifest in the record of deeds.

He sought release from Xuzhou to avoid the crucial post at the northern gate; he bitterly begged for Kuaiji, eager to dwell in the idle duties of eastern Ou—this all is manifest in the record of deeds.
東甌 is Dong'ou on the eastern seaboard; Yong is an unrelated toponym.
At the start of Jianping there was obstruction, and in Yuanhui there was not yet open rebellion—the aim was solely to lay blame on Ruan and Yang, which only deepened the suspicion against the prince.
At the start, Jianping met obstruction, and in Yuanhui there was not yet open rebellion—the aim was solely to lay blame on Ruan and Yang, which only deepened the suspicion against the prince.
建平初阻 is Prince Jianping’s early obstruction, not a Jianping reign; 元徽 is the era name that follows.
At the beginning of Jianping there was obstruction; in Yuanhui there was not yet rebellion—one wished solely to lay blame on Ruan and Yang, which only increased the suspicion incurred.
At the beginning Jianping met obstruction; in Yuanhui there was not yet rebellion—one wished solely to lay blame on Ruan and Yang, which only increased the suspicion incurred.
The literal “beginning of Jianping” likewise treats 建平 as a reign; making Jianping the subject of 阻 matches the Chinese.

The Founding Emperor praised his integrity and made him Recorder, then promoted him through Western Left of the Minister of Works, Attendant of the Household Bureau on the Grand Marshal's staff, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Chief Clerk on Wang Jian's Guard staff.

The Founding Emperor praised his integrity and made him Recorder, then promoted him through Western Left of the Minister of Education, Attendant of the Household Bureau on the Grand Marshal's staff, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Chief Clerk on Wang Jian's Guard staff.
司徒 is Minister of Education (Masses), not Minister of Works (司空).

The Founding Emperor praised his righteousness, transferred him to be Recorder, promoted him to Western Left of the Minister of Works, Attendant of the Household Bureau on the Grand Marshal's staff, Palace Secretariat Attendant, and Chief Clerk on Wang Jian's Guard staff.

The Founding Emperor praised his righteousness, transferred him to be Recorder, promoted him to Western Left of the Minister of Education, Attendant of the Household Bureau on the Grand Marshal's staff, Palace Secretariat Attendant, and Chief Clerk on Wang Jian's Guard staff.
The literal line repeats the 司徒/Minister of Works error.

In the first year of Yongming, Prince Jingling of Ziliang petitioned to establish Companions and Academy officers; Chang was made Literary Scholar to the prince, and they drew together in purity and trust with deep mutual affection.

In the first year of Yongming, Xiao Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, petitioned to establish Companions and Academy officers; Chang was made Literary Scholar to the prince, and they drew together in purity and trust with deep mutual affection.
竟陵王子良 is the Prince of Jingling, given name Ziliang; “of Ziliang” treats the given name as a place. Xiao Ziliang is the Qi princely identity.

In the first year of Yongming, Prince Jingling of Ziliang memorialized to establish Companions and Academy officers; Chang was made Literary Scholar for Prince Jingling; through purity and trust they won each other, and their affection was very deep.

In the first year of Yongming, Xiao Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, memorialized to establish Companions and Academy officers; Chang was made Literary Scholar for Prince Jingling; through purity and trust they won each other, and their affection was very deep.
The literal English has the same title/given-name inversion.
When Prince Linhai of Zhaoxiu held Jing Province, Chang was made his Chief Clerk, General Who Assists the State, and Administrator of Nanjun, with charge of Jing Province affairs.

When Xiao Zhaoxiu, Prince of Linhai, held Jing Province, Chang was made Chief Clerk of the Western Central Commandant, General Who Assists the State, and Administrator of Nanjun, with charge of Jing Province affairs.
昭秀 is the personal name and 西中郎長史 is omitted, but 臨海王昭秀 is a Qi prince of the Xiao house, not Liu. Keep the office restoration and use Xiao.
Yao had four elder brothers—Yang, Tiao, Hao, and Chong—and the world said that Xie Zhuang had named his sons Wind, Moon, Scenery, Mountain, and Water.
Yao had four elder brothers—Yang, Fei, Hao, and Chong—and the world said that Xie Zhuang had named his sons Wind, Moon, Scenery, Mountain, and Water.
朏 is Fei (“new moon”), matching the 月 series; Tiao is a different Xie name (朓).
Yao had four elder brothers Yang, Tiao, Hao, and Chong; the age called Xie Zhuang's naming of his sons Wind, Moon, Scenery, Mountain, and Water.
Yao had four elder brothers Yang, Fei, Hao, and Chong; the age called Xie Zhuang's naming of his sons Wind, Moon, Scenery, Mountain, and Water.
The same 朏 romanization error is in the literal field.
On entering office he became Secretary Attendant and rose to Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the Founding Emperor's Rapid Cavalry staff.
On entering office he became Secretary Attendant and rose to Attendant Gentleman on the Founding Emperor's Rapid Cavalry staff.
太祖驃騎從事中郎 is an adjutant on the Rapid Cavalry staff, not Masters of Writing.
On leaving the sackcloth he became Secretary Attendant and rose to Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the Founding Emperor's Rapid Cavalry staff.
On leaving the sackcloth he became Secretary Attendant and rose to Attendant Gentleman on the Founding Emperor's Rapid Cavalry staff.
The literal rendering invents the same Masters of Writing office for 驃騎從事中郎.
He was soon made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and General of Valiant Cavalry, then Chief Clerk and concurrently Palace Attendant.
He was soon made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and General of Valiant Cavalry, then regular concurrent Palace Attendant.
長兼侍中 is a regular concurrent Palace Attendant post; 長 is not 長史 “Chief Clerk.”
Soon he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry, then Chief Clerk and concurrently Palace Attendant.
Soon he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry, then regular concurrent Palace Attendant.
The literal line repeats the 長兼侍中 / Chief Clerk error.

Later at a court banquet, when meritorious ministers offered wine, Minister of Works Wang Yan and others rose; Yao alone remained seated and said, "Your Majesty received the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people—yet Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own achievement."

Later at a court banquet, when meritorious ministers offered wine, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Yan and others rose; Yao alone remained seated and said, "Your Majesty received the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people—yet Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own achievement."
尚書令 is Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Minister of Works.

Later at a court banquet, when meritorious ministers offered wine, Minister of Works Wang Yan and others rose from their seats; Yao alone did not rise and said: "Your Majesty received the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people—Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own power."

Later at a court banquet, when meritorious ministers offered wine, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Yan and others rose from their seats; Yao alone did not rise and said: "Your Majesty received the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people—Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own power."
The literal line has the same 尚書令 error.
When the banquet ended, Yan invited Yao to ride back with him to the Ministry of Works, hoping to win him over.
When the banquet ended, Yan invited Yao to ride back with him to the Directorate of the Imperial Secretariat, hoping to win him over.
令省 is the office of the 尚書令, not the Ministry of Works.
When the seating ended, Yan called Yao to ride together back to the Ministry of Works, wishing to soothe and please him.
When the seating ended, Yan called Yao to ride together back to the office of the Director of the Imperial Secretariat, wishing to soothe and please him.
The literal “Ministry of Works” for 令省 is the same misidentification of the Shangshu ling’s office.
In the first year of Yongtai he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattershot Cavalry and Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
